newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Ratio spread and cylinder traded in BP.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Ratio spread and cylinder traded in BP.

text.p: The risk of further falls in British Petroleum shares allowed traders to adopt complex options stratgies on Wednesday, dealers said.
One was a two-for-one ratio put spread and another was a short cylinder.
For the put spread, 2,000 April 650 puts were sold at 5p while 1,000 April 700 puts were bought at 18-1/2p for a net debit of 8-1/2p.
A maximum profit of 41-1/2p will be made if BP shares are 650p at expiry. Above 700p, the losses will be limited to 8-1/2p and if the shares fall too far the losses will increase.
The other large deal in British Petroleum involved selling 1,000 July 700 puts at 30p and buying 1,000 July 750 calls at 33-1/2p for a net debit of 3-1/2p.
In addition, dealers believed a million BP shares were also sold at 721-3/4p, making this a short cylinder strategy.

The position is bearish since the underlying shares were sold. But as a hedge against the stock price rising, call options were purchased. So if BP shares go anywhere above 750p, the long calls can be exercised to buy shares at 750p.
And if the shares fall below 700p, the trader may have to buy the shares back at 700p owing to possible assignment.
By 1445 GMT, BP shares had fallen 6-1/2p to 722p.

Over in satellite television broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting a bullish position was rolled forward. It involved selling 1,000 March 550 calls at 44p in a closing deal and buying 1,000 March 600 calls at 19p.
Two-way trading in April/October calendar spreads accounted for the main deals in pharmaceuticals group Glaxo Wellcome whose shares were down 7p to 959p.
